claim: V1 interneurons originate from p1 progenitors and express the transcription factor Engrailed-1 (En1).
source: We focus here on one major group of ventral inhibitory interneurons known as V1 that originate from p1 progenitors, express the transcription factor (TF) Engrailed-1 (En1), and send ipsilateral axons throughout the ventral horn including lamina IX (LIX), where they densely innervate motoneuron cell bodies and proximal dendrites (Alvarez et al., 2005; Goulding, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Alvarez et al., 2005; Goulding, 2009) establishing these characteristics of V1 interneurons.

claim: V1 interneurons play crucial roles shaping motor output and modulating locomotor speed.
source: Electrophysiological and modeling studies then showed that V1 interneurons play crucial roles shaping motor output and modulating locomotor speed, governing flexion-extension at the level of central pattern generator half-centers and/or last-order reciprocal inhibition of antagonistic motoneurons and providing recurrent feedback inhibition of motoneuron firing (Sapir et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 2014; Britz et al., 2015; Falgairolle and O'Donovan, 2019; Falgairolle and O'Donovan, 2021; Shevtsova et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple electrophysiological and modeling studies (Sapir et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 2014; Britz et al., 2015; Falgairolle and O'Donovan, 2019; Falgairolle and O'Donovan, 2021; Shevtsova et al., 2022).

evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by genetic lineage labeling across different segments shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Only around half of genetically identified Foxp2-V1 cells were Foxp2 immunolabeled at P5.
source: Correspondingly, only around half of genetically identified Foxp2-V1 cells were Foxp2 immunolabeled at P5 in dual-color R26 RCE:dualEGFP/Ai9-lsl-tdT mice (Figure 3F, n=2 mice, 3 ventral horns each) or in single-color R26 RCE:dualEGFP mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, n=3 mice, 4 ventral horns each).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by comparison of genetic lineage labeling and Foxp2 immunoreactivity at P5 shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Lineage labeled Foxp2-V1 cells did not express markers of other V1 clades.
source: Lineage labeled Foxp2-V1 cells did not express markers of other V1 clades, suggesting they uniquely represent the Foxp2-V1 clade.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by immunolabeling for other V1 clade markers in genetically labeled Foxp2-V1 cells shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Non-Foxp2 tdT-only V1 cells expressed all other clade-specific TFs (Pou6f2, MafB, and Sp8) and consistently lacked Foxp2 immunoreactivity.
source: Non-Foxp2 tdT-only V1 cells expressed all other clade-specific TFs (Pou6f2, MafB, and Sp8) and consistently lacked Foxp2 immunoreactivity (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by immunolabeling for V1 clade markers in genetically labeled non-Foxp2-V1 cells shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Lineage-labeled Foxp2-V1 interneurons comprise 55.7%±4.7 (mean ± SD) of all spinal cord Foxp2+ neurons at P5 (n=4 mice).
source: Overall, lineage-labeled Foxp2-V1 interneurons comprise 55.7%±4.7 (mean ± SD) of all spinal cord Foxp2+ neurons at P5 (n=4 mice, 2 P5 and 2 P20, Figure 3J).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of Foxp2-V1 cells among all Foxp2+ neurons shown in Figure 3J.

claim: Foxp2-V1 interneuron numbers significantly increase in segments innervating limb muscles (L3-L6) compared to segments involved with axial (Th13, S1) and hypaxial muscles (L1).
source: Correspondingly, Foxp2-V1 neuron numbers significantly increase in segments innervating limb muscles (L3-L6) compared to segments involved with axial (Th13, S1) and hypaxial muscles (L1) (p<0.0001, one-way ANOVA followed by post hoc Bonferroni t-tests summarized in Figure 4D and Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of Foxp2-V1 cells across spinal segments shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The ratio of Foxp2-V1 interneurons to motoneurons remained relatively constant from Th13 to L5.
source: Consistent with the parallel increase in number of V1 interneurons and motoneurons, the ratio of Foxp2-V1 interneurons to motoneurons remained relatively constant from Th13 to L5 (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of Foxp2-V1 to motoneuron ratios across spinal segments shown in Figure 4E.

claim: HMC and lower lumbar LMC motoneurons receive significantly more V1 synapses than MMC motoneurons.
source: Post hoc Bonferroni t-tests demonstrated that HMC and lower lumbar LMC motoneurons receive significantly more V1 synapses than MMC motoneurons, while LMC motoneurons in L1/2 and L6 had V1 synaptic densities not significantly different to MMC motoneurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of V1 synapse densities on different motoneuron types shown in Figure 5D.

claim: LMC motoneurons in L1/2 and L6 had V1 synaptic densities not significantly different to MMC motoneurons.
source: Post hoc Bonferroni t-tests demonstrated that HMC and lower lumbar LMC motoneurons receive significantly more V1 synapses than MMC motoneurons, while LMC motoneurons in L1/2 and L6 had V1 synaptic densities not significantly different to MMC motoneurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of V1 synapse densities on different motoneuron types shown in Figure 5D.

claim: PGC neurons received very low densities of V1 input, significantly lower than LMC or MMC motoneurons.
source: PGC neurons received very low densities of V1 input, significantly lower than LMC or MMC motoneurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of V1 synapse densities on PGC neurons shown in Figure 5D.

claim: HMC and LMC motoneurons receive significantly higher synaptic densities of Foxp2-V1 axons compared to non-Foxp2-V1 axons in all segments, except for L1/2.
source: HMC and LMC motoneurons receive significantly higher synaptic densities of Foxp2-V1 axons compared to non-Foxp2-V1 axons in all segments, except for L1/2.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of Foxp2-V1 vs non-Foxp2-V1 synapse densities on different motoneuron types shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The synaptic densities of Foxp2-V1 and non-Foxp2-V1 axons are not significantly different in MMC motoneurons, except for S1 MMC motoneurons that received significantly higher density of non-Foxp2-V1 synapses.
source: The synaptic densities of both types of axons are not significantly different in MMC motoneurons, except for S1 MMC motoneurons that received significantly higher density of non-Foxp2-V1 synapses.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of Foxp2-V1 vs non-Foxp2-V1 synapse densities on MMC motoneurons shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Renshaw cell synapses occurred at significantly lower densities compared to Foxp2-V1s in all LMC motor groups, except for L1/2.
source: Post hoc pairwise comparisons revealed that Renshaw cell synapses occurred at significantly lower densities compared to Foxp2-V1s in all LMC motor groups, except for L1/2 (Figure 5E, lower graph).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of Renshaw cell vs Foxp2-V1 synapse densities on LMC motoneurons shown in Figure 5E.

claim: MMC motoneurons showed similar densities of Renshaw cell and Foxp2-V1 synapses in Th13 and L1/2, higher density of Foxp2-V1 synapses in L3/4, and much higher density of calbindin+ V1 synapses in S1.
source: MMC motoneurons showed similar densities of Renshaw cell and Foxp2-V1 synapses in Th13 and L1/2, higher density of Foxp2-V1 synapses in L3/4, and much higher density of calbindin+ V1 synapses in S1.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of Renshaw cell vs Foxp2-V1 synapse densities on MMC motoneurons shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Most synapses on the cell bodies of HMC, LMC, and MMC motoneurons originate from either Foxp2-V1s or Renshaw cells.
source: Plotting the percent contributions of three V1 synapse categories to all V1 synapses shows that most synapses on the cell bodies of HMC, LMC, and MMC motoneurons originate from either Foxp2-V1s or Renshaw cells (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of V1 synapse contributions shown in Figure 5F.

claim: PGC neurons mostly receive inputs from V1s that are non-Foxp2 and non-Renshaw cells, but the frequency of these synapses is very low and highly variable.
source: PGC neurons mostly receive inputs from V1s that are non-Foxp2 and non-Renshaw cells, but the frequency of these synapses is very low and highly variable.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of V1 synapse contributions on PGC neurons shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Around 50% of lineage-labeled Foxp2-V1 interneurons express Otp at P5.
source: Otp was expressed in around 50% of lineage-labeled Foxp2-V1 interneurons, and Foxp4 in 20%.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of Otp expression in Foxp2-V1 cells shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Around 20% of lineage-labeled Foxp2-V1 interneurons express Foxp4 at P5.
source: Otp was expressed in around 50% of lineage-labeled Foxp2-V1 interneurons, and Foxp4 in 20%.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of Foxp4 expression in Foxp2-V1 cells shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Foxp4-IR/Foxp2-V1 interneurons always co-localized with Otp-IR, indicating they are a subpopulation of the Otp group.
source: Foxp4-IR/Foxp2-V1 interneurons always co-localized with Otp-IR, indicating they are a subpopulation of the Otp group.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by co-localization analyses shown in Figure 6A.

claim: A large group of Foxp2-V1 cells that co-expresses Otp and Foxp2 at P5 (44% of Foxp2-V1 cells) is localized close to the LMC.
source: To summarize the most salient results, a large group of Foxp2-V1 cells that co-expresses Otp and Foxp2 at P5 (44% of Foxp2-V1 cells) is localized close to the LMC.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification and localization of Otp and Foxp2 co-expressing Foxp2-V1 cells shown in Figure 6C.

claim: A smaller subgroup of Foxp2-V1 cells located more ventrally also expresses Foxp4 (23% of Foxp2-V1 cells).
source: It includes a smaller subgroup located more ventrally that also expresses Foxp4 (23% of Foxp2-V1 cells).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification and localization of Otp, Foxp2, and Foxp4 co-expressing Foxp2-V1 cells shown in Figure 6C.

claim: 63.0% and 74.3% of Foxp2-V1 interneurons received VGLUT1 synapses in each animal respectively.
source: Overall, we found that 63.0% and 74.3% of Foxp2-V1 interneurons received VGLUT1 synapses in each animal respectively (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of VGLUT1 synapses on Foxp2-V1 cells shown in Figure 7C.

claim: VGLUT1 synapses preferentially targeted genetically labeled Foxp2-V1 interneurons expressing Otp and Foxp2 at P5.
source: VGLUT1 synapses preferentially targeted genetically labeled Foxp2-V1 interneurons expressing Otp and Foxp2 at P5 (Figure 7C and D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of VGLUT1 synapses on Otp and Foxp2 expressing Foxp2-V1 cells shown in Figure 7C and D.

claim: 65.8% of interneurons receiving VGLUT1 synapses in the Foxp2-V1 lineage express Otp.
source: On average (n=2 mice, 12 ventral horns and 1116 Foxp2-V1 cells analyzed), 42.5% of Foxp2-V1 interneurons had VGLUT1 contacts and were Otp+, while 22.1% were Otp(-). Thus, 65.8% of interneurons receiving VGLUT1 synapses in the Foxp2-V1 lineage express Otp.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of Otp expression in VGLUT1-contacted Foxp2-V1 cells shown in Figure 7D.

claim: VGLUT1 synapses contacted 82.0% of Otp+ Foxp2 V1 interneurons.
source: Thus, VGLUT1 synapses contacted 82.0% of Otp+ Foxp2 V1 interneurons and 64.9% received these synapses proximally (cell body and primary dendrites) in addition to also having VGLUT1 synapses on more distal dendrites.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of VGLUT1 synapses on Otp+ Foxp2-V1 cells shown in Figure 7D.

claim: 68.7% of interneurons in the Foxp2-V1 lineage that were targeted by VGLUT1 synapses had Foxp2 expression at P5.
source: This suggests that 68.7% of interneurons in the Foxp2-V1 lineage that were targeted by VGLUT1 synapses had Foxp2 expression at P5, and therefore 73.3% of Foxp2-V1 interneurons with genetic and antibody labeling received VGLUT1 synapses.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of Foxp2 expression in VGLUT1-contacted Foxp2-V1 cells shown in Figure 7D.

claim: 85.6% of Otp+ cells receiving VGLUT1 synapses in the Foxp2-V1 lineage also maintain Foxp2 expression at P5.
source: In one of the two animals we also analyzed Otp and Foxp2 co-localization in Foxp2-V1 interneurons receiving VGLUT1+ synapses. We found that 85.6% of Otp+ cells receiving VGLUT1 synapses in the Foxp2-V1 lineage also maintain Foxp2 expression at P5, while 89.8% of genetic and Foxp2 antibody labeled V1s receiving VGLUT1 synapses are also Otp+.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of Otp and Foxp2 co-expression in VGLUT1-contacted Foxp2-V1 cells.

claim: 89.8% of genetic and Foxp2 antibody labeled V1s receiving VGLUT1 synapses are also Otp+.
source: In one of the two animals we also analyzed Otp and Foxp2 co-localization in Foxp2-V1 interneurons receiving VGLUT1+ synapses. We found that 85.6% of Otp+ cells receiving VGLUT1 synapses in the Foxp2-V1 lineage also maintain Foxp2 expression at P5, while 89.8% of genetic and Foxp2 antibody labeled V1s receiving VGLUT1 synapses are also Otp+.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by quantification of Otp and Foxp2 co-expression in VGLUT1-contacted Foxp2-V1 cells.

claim: Birthdate order was not predictive of presynaptic coupling to motoneurons or phylogenetic relations.
source: It is notable that birthdate order was not predictive of presynaptic coupling to motoneurons or phylogenetic relations.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing that both early and late born V1 clades can be tightly coupled to motoneurons.

claim: Reciprocal inhibition of muscle flexors and extensors at limb joints first appears in limbed Amphibia, a subclass of tetrapodal vertebrates that lacks recurrent inhibitory circuits.
source: Reciprocal inhibition of muscle flexors and extensors at limb joints first appears in limbed Amphibia, a subclass of tetrapodal vertebrates that lacks recurrent inhibitory circuits (Czéh, 1977).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Czéh, 1977).

claim: Recurrent inhibition of motoneurons by Renshaw cells has only been detected in mammals and in the developing hindlimb motor pools of chick embryos.
source: At present recurrent inhibition of motoneurons by Renshaw cells has only been detected in mammals and in the developing hindlimb motor pools of chick embryos (Wenner and O'Donovan, 1999; Alvarez and Fyffe, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Wenner and O'Donovan, 1999; Alvarez and Fyffe, 2007).

claim: V1 interneurons are found in all vertebrate species ranging from fishes with swimming locomotion to mammals with limbed terrestrial locomotion.
source: V1 interneurons are found in all vertebrate species ranging from fishes with swimming locomotion to mammals with limbed terrestrial locomotion, but while V1 interneurons show low diversity in zebrafish (Kimura and Higashijima, 2019) they display large heterogeneity in mice (Bikoff et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Kimura and Higashijima, 2019; Bikoff et al., 2016).

claim: V1 interneurons show low diversity in zebrafish.
source: V1 interneurons are found in all vertebrate species ranging from fishes with swimming locomotion to mammals with limbed terrestrial locomotion, but while V1 interneurons show low diversity in zebrafish (Kimura and Higashijima, 2019) they display large heterogeneity in mice (Bikoff et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Kimura and Higashijima, 2019).

claim: V1 interneurons display large heterogeneity in mice.
source: V1 interneurons are found in all vertebrate species ranging from fishes with swimming locomotion to mammals with limbed terrestrial locomotion, but while V1 interneurons show low diversity in zebrafish (Kimura and Higashijima, 2019) they display large heterogeneity in mice (Bikoff et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Bikoff et al., 2016).

claim: Thoracic axial motoneurons in the cat are modulated by Renshaw cell-mediated recurrent inhibition.
source: These motoneurons are densely innervated by Foxp2-V1s and Renshaw cells and correspondingly, thoracic axial motoneurons in the cat are modulated by Renshaw cell-mediated recurrent inhibition (Saywell et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Saywell et al., 2013).

claim: Renshaw cells and subgroups of Foxp2-V1s involved in reciprocal inhibitory circuits together with flexor and extensor motoneurons form a canonical motor output module that controls the muscles around individual joints.
source: Together with flexor and extensor motoneurons, these cells form a canonical motor output module that controls the muscles around individual joints. This canonical microcircuit was first proposed by Baldissera et al., 1981, as an end-stage modulator of the spatiotemporal properties of the motor output across all spinal segments in all mammalian species (human and cats at the time, and now also rats and mice).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Baldissera et al., 1981).

claim: V1 synapses located on the cell bodies and proximal dendrites of motoneurons are preferentially affected during early stages of ALS.
source: These studies showed that V1 synapses located on the cell bodies and proximal dendrites of motoneurons are preferentially affected during early stages of the disease, and in addition Foxp2-V1 interneurons have a high susceptibility for cell death (Wootz et al., 2013; Salamatina et al., 2020; Montañana-Rosell et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies (Wootz et al., 2013; Salamatina et al., 2020; Montañana-Rosell et al., 2024).

claim: Foxp2-V1 interneurons have a high susceptibility for cell death in ALS.
source: These studies showed that V1 synapses located on the cell bodies and proximal dendrites of motoneurons are preferentially affected during early stages of the disease, and in addition Foxp2-V1 interneurons have a high susceptibility for cell death (Wootz et al., 2013; Salamatina et al., 2020; Montañana-Rosell et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies (Wootz et al., 2013; Salamatina et al., 2020; Montañana-Rosell et al., 2024).

claim: Renshaw cells are burst-tonic firing cells.
source: Renshaw cells are burst-tonic firing cells, while Foxp2-V1 interneurons are tonic fast-spiking (Bikoff et al., 2016) with these properties further diverging during postnatal maturation.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Bikoff et al., 2016).

claim: Foxp2-V1 interneurons are tonic fast-spiking.
source: Renshaw cells are burst-tonic firing cells, while Foxp2-V1 interneurons are tonic fast-spiking (Bikoff et al., 2016) with these properties further diverging during postnatal maturation.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Bikoff et al., 2016).

claim: 24 hr treatment with a high concentration of retinoic acid and a low concentration of smoothened agonist induced mESC derivation of p1 progenitors.
source: In a remarkable in vitro replication of the V1 neurogenesis sequence using mouse embryonic stem cells (mESC), it was found that 24 hr treatment with a high concentration of retinoic acid and a low concentration of smoothened agonist induced mESC derivation of p1 progenitors (Hoang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Hoang et al., 2018).

claim: p1 progenitors sequentially generated V1 interneurons with genetic profiles of Renshaw cells at in vitro day 5 and Foxp2-V1s at day 8.
source: These progenitors sequentially generated V1 interneurons with genetic profiles of Renshaw cells at in vitro day 5 and Foxp2-V1s at day 8.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Hoang et al., 2018).

claim: Lengthening the retinoic acid treatment favored differentiation into neurons with Renshaw cell characteristics at the expense of Foxp2-V1s.
source: Lengthening the retinoic acid treatment favored differentiation into neurons with Renshaw cell characteristics at the expense of Foxp2-V1s.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Hoang et al., 2018).

claim: In early embryos retinoic acid is highly expressed by the mesoderm adjacent to the developing spinal cord and by motoneurons inside the spinal cord.
source: For example, in early embryos retinoic acid is highly expressed by the mesoderm adjacent to the developing spinal cord (Novitch et al., 2003) and by motoneurons inside the spinal cord (Sockanathan et al., 2003), but retinoic acid signals are later attenuated by opposing actions from fibroblast growth factor family members (Diez del Corral et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Novitch et al., 2003; Sockanathan et al., 2003).

claim: Retinoic acid signals are later attenuated by opposing actions from fibroblast growth factor family members.
source: For example, in early embryos retinoic acid is highly expressed by the mesoderm adjacent to the developing spinal cord (Novitch et al., 2003) and by motoneurons inside the spinal cord (Sockanathan et al., 2003), but retinoic acid signals are later attenuated by opposing actions from fibroblast growth factor family members (Diez del Corral et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Diez del Corral et al., 2003).
